about: One entry per normative clause the baseline evals target. Coverage is derived from evals/*.json: automated, manual (documented observation), conditional (engine-dependent), optional (MAY, not gated), absent (MUST/SHOULD with no case).
quirks: Section number 14 is used twice in the spec (Code Execution Runtime and Durable Key-Value Store). KV requirements use the id prefix S14K and section 14.
Section 16 links code execution as #13-code-execution-runtime, which points at the wrong section number. Requirements are cited from sections 14.1-14.9 instead.

requirements.text: Execute one step at a time per thread.
Persist messages and tool results before continuing.
Enforce configured limits and stop semantics.
Support queued work for idle and active threads.
Expose ThreadState.decide() and make it available when state.execution is null.
Start execution on each listed trigger: user message, queueMessage, queueTool, scheduled effect.
Queue new work while executing; start a new execution when idle.
Run the seven prompt-side steps in order: drain, assemble, call model, persist response, tools, persist results, stops.
Handler-backed turn is one handler invocation: no context assembly, no model call, exactly-once and in order.
Human-backed turn parks execution until the inbound message arrives.
Assemble in order: interpolate system, after_system_message, snapshot, filter_messages once, provider messages, prefilter_llm_history, dispatch.
Snapshot eligibility: messages persisted before filter_messages are eligible now; later injections wait for the next assembly.
injectMessage() must not restart snapshot/filter/prefilter; live history stays independent of request context.
Silent messages remain eligible for the context snapshot.
Perspective mapping: own turns are assistant, opposite side is user, opposite-side tool calls are not visible.
requirements.note: `api-11-perspective-mapping` renders one history through both sides of `dual_agent`; `scripted_dual` records each call's provider rows in `model.views`.

requirements.text: Attachments remain multimodal content when the model supports it.
requirements.note: `api-08-attachment-parts` sends a PNG to `scripted_vision` (declares `capabilities.supportsImages`) and asserts the provider request carries an image part and the persisted message keeps the attachment.

requirements.text: Execute tool calls sequentially in the order returned.
Persist tool errors as tool results without crashing the execution loop.
Support function tools, prompt tools, agent handoff tools, and injected subagent lifecycle tools.
Evaluate stops in order: sessionStop/sessionFail, stopTool, stopOnResponse, safety limits.
Create children with parent linkage, registry entries keyed by relationship name, and ThreadState lookup.
Inject subagents, subagent_create, subagent_message for non-hidden prompt-side relationships.
Exceeding maxInstances returns a tool error with actionable guidance.
Effective parentCommunication defaults to implicit; explicit children do not auto-queue completion to the parent and do not wake it.
optional relationships activate only when the env flag resolves to true, 1, or yes (case-insensitive).
immediate relationships spawn at thread creation before any side takes a turn, including for handler-owned sides.
hidden relationships stay spawnable by runtime code but never appear in an LLM tool list.
Immediate object form: only nameEnv/descriptionEnv are model-visible; scopedEnv stays runtime-only.
Immediate spawning is recursive across activated child threads.
Resolve the complete thread-hook set from enabled direct relationships before a hook position runs; fail closed if a required hook cannot load or is user-scoped.
requirements.note: Two cases over `fixtures-broken/`: a required hook id nothing defines (`api-09-parent-hook-missing`) and a user-scope hook id (`api-09-parent-hook-user-scoped`, red until the loader check landed).

requirements.text: Within a position: child before_parent hooks, then the parent hook set, then child after_parent hooks, each in stable order.
Map relationship payloads to initial user message, initial attachments, and child name.
subagent_create requires a non-empty name argument.
subagent_create.arguments are validated against the child side A requiredSchema.
Persist initial arguments and expose them to both child sides via ThreadState.arguments and prompt interpolation.
Missing scoped variables return a structured bootstrap error plus GET/POST variable endpoints.
requirements.note: Needs the thread HTTP routes, covered by the manual client-API suite.

requirements.text: Copy referenced attachments parent to child; queued child messages use child-local paths.
Convert child sessionStop/sessionFail to a parent queued message, copy payload attachments child to parent, include reference and summary.
notifyParent, setStatus, and stopSession work for explicit children as escalation.
Without a parent, notifyParent queues nothing externally and setStatus is a no-op.
sessionStatus updates registry status without terminating the child.
stopSession marks the session terminal without a sessionStop tool call and counts as a successful child run.
Queued messages are durable and ordered: inject before the next model call, FIFO, force a turn when idle.
Queued work survives durable-object eviction.
requirements.note: `api-06-eviction-queue-durable` queues two messages without triggering, then restarts the Runtime over the same store and asserts both entries in order. No resume claim: the spec does not say how an evicted object wakes.

requirements.text: terminate() is soft shutdown: set terminated timestamp, abort in-flight work, reject future execute/queue/send, propagate to parent registry.
Session end (stop, fail, error, turn cap) must not terminate a child thread.
A single thread never runs concurrent flows; cross-thread concurrency is allowed.
Persist synthesized status messages with metadata.status_kind.
When runtime streams are implemented they route to the selected host, do not park, and terminate on host disconnect.
requirements.note: Optional capability with its own live-stream contract; needs the stream harness.

requirements.text: Create a fresh isolate per runCode call with no leaked module cache, intrinsics, or bindings.
globalThis exposes only ECMAScript intrinsics; no fetch, setTimeout, console, process, or require.
Install options.globals at module scope only, never on globalThis.
Freshly construct intrinsic prototypes; sandbox mutations do not affect the host.
Reject eval, new Function(source), SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics, and URL dynamic imports.
Bare specifiers resolve only from options.imports; relative only from options.modules; unknown and URL specifiers fail with link_error.
imports entries are synthetic modules with frozen namespace copies; default key becomes the default export.
import.meta.url is a synthetic sandbox: filename URL, never a host path.
Primitives cross the boundary by value.
Plain objects, arrays, Map, Set, Date, and typed arrays cross by structured clone with no shared reference.
Functions cross as callable proxies that await returned promises.
Reject non-transferable values (class instances, WeakMap, WeakRef, host symbols) with SerializationError.
Bridged functions expose no host this or closure state beyond explicit arguments.
Enforce options.memoryLimitBytes and settle with status memory on overrun when the engine supports heap accounting.
Document the runtime-defined default memory limit.
requirements.note: Documentation check, not observable from an eval run. The default (64 MiB) is stated under 'This runtime' in rules/ADRs/code-execution-resource-limits-and-termination.md.

requirements.text: Above a platform ceiling, either clamp and settle with memory naming the effective limit, or reject with link_error naming the cap; document which and the ceiling.
requirements.note: Documentation plus a platform-cap configuration not exposed by the fixture. The reference runtime clamps above 2 GiB and names the effective limit; see 'This runtime' in rules/ADRs/code-execution-resource-limits-and-termination.md.

requirements.text: handle.terminate() settles at the next yield point, SHOULD be within 50 ms, and typically a few.
terminate is idempotent; later calls are no-ops.
A caller-supplied terminate reason surfaces in result.error.message.
Optional safety caps settle with status terminated and a diagnosable message.
No wall-clock timeout is invented silently; callers impose deadlines via terminate.
Resolve the selected export in the fixed order: read namespace[fn], call if function, await thenables, marshal.
Missing selected export settles with link_error.
Selected export that is not a function with non-empty args settles with error.
An uncaught throw or rejected promise from the selected export settles with error.
TypeScript is the default language and is erased before evaluation; no type-checker runs.
The sandbox has its own microtask queue; Promise and await behave normally.
setTimeout and setInterval are absent unless bridged through options.globals.
Top-level await is supported; the module completes when evaluation and export resolution settle.
Expose ThreadState.runCode(source, options?) returning a CodeExecution handle.
requirements.note: Implicitly exercised by every code-execution case.

requirements.text: Return CodeExecutionResult with exactly the status codes of the caller-facing spec.
requirements.note: Assertions use success, error, link_error, terminated, and memory.

requirements.text: Capture console.* logs when no console global is supplied.
Surface syntactic and linker errors with line/column pointing at the caller source.
Call handle.terminate() when state.execution.abortSignal fires.
getValue/setValue persist to durable per-thread storage surviving execution and process boundaries.
A written value is visible to every subsequent getValue on the same thread, across tools, hooks, and endpoints.
Each thread has an isolated key space; no parent, child, or sibling can read it.
Values round-trip JSON-equivalent structure; non-JSON values may be rejected.
getValue returns null for a missing or deleted key.
setValue(key, null) and setValue(key, undefined) delete the key.
Writes are durable before the setValue promise resolves.
Values are not copied, inherited, or synchronized when subagents are spawned.
Encryption at rest is optional for the store.
Implementation-defined caps on key length, value size, and key count.
Expose the Thread Client API.
requirements.note: Route surface is exercised by the manual client-API suite.

requirements.text: Mount every specified route beneath the runtime prefix.
requirements.note: Needs an HTTP client against a running runtime.

requirements.text: Authenticate every request, accept bearer credentials and single-use stream tickets, enforce thread access policy.
requirements.note: Needs an HTTP/WS client and a runtime with auth configured.

requirements.text: Return 5xx, never a client-error status, for internal failures.
requirements.note: Needs fault injection at the HTTP boundary.

requirements.text: Set a created thread owner from the authenticated caller.
requirements.note: Needs an HTTP client.

requirements.text: Accept a sent message durably and respond before the resulting execution completes.
requirements.note: Needs an HTTP client and a slow execution.

requirements.text: Send a thread_status snapshot as the first frame and again on every run status change.
requirements.note: Needs a WebSocket client.

requirements.text: Publish message_data, message_chunk, and event frames.
requirements.note: Needs a WebSocket client.

requirements.text: Withhold reasoning_chunk frames from connections that did not opt in.
requirements.note: Needs a WebSocket client and a model that returns reasoning.

requirements.text: Persist model reasoning with the assistant message and carry it on reads and on the stream.
requirements.note: Needs a model that returns reasoning plus HTTP reads.

requirements.text: On thread deletion, make the thread and descendants unavailable, abort and discard work, close streams before confirming.
requirements.note: Needs an HTTP/WS client.

requirements.text: Apply each connection depth and includeSilent filters.
requirements.note: Needs a WebSocket client.

requirements.text: Answer stream_ping with stream_pong.
requirements.note: Needs a WebSocket client.
